authority: New Hampshire Department of Environmental Services
reader_title: How much land will grading disturb?
summary: New Hampshire counts earthmoving over ten years. Disturbing more than 100,000 square feet meets one test for significant terrain alteration; the threshold falls to 50,000 if any of the disturbance is in protected shoreland. Other triggers and permit-by-rule provisions can apply.
locator:
Env-Wq
1502.60(b), significant terrain alteration; Env-Wq 1503 for permit procedures
evidence: cumulatively exceeds 100,000 square feet of area

thresholds.context: Ten-year cumulative disturbance; general area test
Ten-year cumulative disturbance; any portion within protected shoreland

reader_title: A permit to begin operating a nonresidential building
summary: Puerto Rico’s permit office directs new and existing nonresidential buildings and businesses to obtain a Permiso Único to begin or continue operations. This is separate from the permit for construction.
locator: OGPe manual for a new Permiso Único, PDF p. 12
evidence: el Permiso Único para iniciar o continuar sus operaciones

reader_title: When a building needs a new occupancy certificate
summary: The District calls for a new certificate of occupancy after new construction or alteration, or a change in ownership, occupancy load or use. The certificate checks the building’s use against zoning and building codes.
locator: Overview of Permitting Process, Certificate of Occupancy
evidence: A new C of O is required when new construction or alteration has occurred

reader_title: Energy documents for a commercial building application
summary: For new construction, additions and Level 3 alterations, the District requires an energy worksheet through January 31, 2027. Commercial-code applicants may instead use COMcheck for energy compliance and select the DC 2017 Energy Code.
locator: Energy and Green Worksheets Workbook, first paragraph and commercial exception
evidence: Permit applications subject to the commercial code may opt to use COMcheck
